title: AIC: A Global View: Recent Acquisitions of Textiles, 2012–2016
theme: A Global View: Recent Acquisitions of Textiles, 2012–2016
description: This selection of 39 works showcases a remarkable variety of cultures, periods, and textile types, mirroring the encyclopedic scope of the museum as a whole.

title: AIC: America after the Fall: Painting in the 1930s
theme: America after the Fall: Painting in the 1930s
description: Featuring works by Edward Hopper, Georgia O’Keeffe, and Grant Wood, this exhibition examines how artists redefined modernism while searching for a national art during the Great Depression.

title: AIC: Vanishing Beauty: Asian Jewelry and Ritual Objects from the Barbara and David Kipper Collection
theme: Vanishing Beauty: Asian Jewelry and Ritual Objects from the Barbara and David Kipper Collection
description: More than 300 highlights from this outstanding collection introduce visitors to exquisite meaning-filled objects and the fast-disappearing cultures that produced them.

title: AIC: Aaron Siskind: Abstractions
description: Featuring 100 photographs, this exhibition examines some of the artist's most influential abstract photographs and series—work that explores what he called “the drama of objects.”

title: AIC: Invisible Man: Gordon Parks and Ralph Ellison in Harlem
theme: Invisible Man: Gordon Parks and Ralph Ellison in Harlem
description: Exploring the little-known collaboration of Parks and Ellison, this exhibition reunites the never-before-seen photographs and unpublished manuscripts intended for two projects.

title: AIC: Van Dyck, Rembrandt, and the Portrait Print
theme: Van Dyck, Rembrandt, and the Portrait Print
description: Inspired by Van Dyck's "Iconography" etchings, this exhibition examines the history of the portrait print through 140 works—from Dürer, Van Dyck, and Rembrandt through Degas, Kollwitz, and Close.

title: AIC: Design Episodes: The Modern Chair
description: The first installment of this series presents iconic chairs by makers including Le Corbusier and Charlotte Perriand, Harry Bertoia, and Charles and Ray Eames.

title: AIC: Kemang Wa Lehulere: In All My Wildest Dreams
theme: Kemang Wa Lehulere: In All My Wildest Dreams
description: The first American museum exhibition devoted to this contemporary South African artist demonstrates the artist’s masterful conflation of personal and collective storytelling.

title: AIC: Abstract/Object
description: A companion to the concurrent Moholy-Nagy retrospective, this exhibition of contemporary work examines the influence the artist had on the field of photography.

title: AIC: Master Drawings Unveiled: 25 Years of Major Acquisitions
theme: Master Drawings Unveiled: 25 Years of Major Acquisitions
description: This celebration of drawings acquired over the last quarter-century presents works of Swiss, German, and Austrian Romanticism; Belgian Symbolism; French Impressionism; and 20th-century American art.

title: AIC: Moholy-Nagy: Future Present
description: The first retrospective of Moholy-Nagy in the United States in nearly 50 years traces the career of a multimedia artist who was always ahead of his time.

title: AIC: Modern Velvet: A Sense of Luxury in the Age of Industry
theme: Modern Velvet: A Sense of Luxury in the Age of Industry
description: Featuring 42 velvets from the 19th century to the present, this exhibition examines the effects of industry on the design and production of a fabric long associated with status and luxury.

title: AIC: Dress Codes: Portrait Photographs from the Collection
theme: Dress Codes: Portrait Photographs from the Collection
description: This exhibition presents five series—from the 1870s to the present—that exemplify the power of clothing to shape identities in front of the camera.

title: AIC: Andrew Lord: Unslumbrous Night
description: This new series of bronze and ceramic sculptures by British artist Andrew Lord was inspired by 19th- and 20th-century paintings that portray time passing and the fragility of the human condition.

title: AIC: Making Memories: Quilts as Souvenirs
description: This presentation of 27 quilts explores the way these textiles function as keepsakes and considers how their material fabrication mimics the construction of memory.

title: AIC: Along the Lines: Selected Drawings by Saul Steinberg
theme: Along the Lines: Selected Drawings by Saul Steinberg
description: As a cartoonist and independent artist, Saul Steinberg crafted a rich and ever-evolving idiom, giving graphic definition to the postwar age.

title: AIC: Shockingly Mad: Henry Fuseli and the Art of Drawing
theme: Shockingly Mad: Henry Fuseli and the Art of Drawing
description: This rich selection of Fuseli’s drawings and prints showcases his passionate and singular approach to drawing, born of political revolutions and radical aesthetic shifts.

title: AIC: Rodin: Sculptor and Storyteller
description: This focused exhibition brings together sculptures and drawings from private collections and the museum’s holdings to explore the artist’s creative process and his narrative skill.

title: AIC: Revoliutsiia! Demonstratsiia! Soviet Art Put to the Test
theme: Revoliutsiia! Demonstratsiia! Soviet Art Put to the Test
description: This exhibition explores the trajectory of early Soviet art in all its forms and what it tells us about socially minded art now.

title: AIC: Cauleen Smith: Human_3.0 Reading List
description: In this series of 57 drawings, Cauleen Smith proposes a new canon of humanistic literacy that is both personal and idiosyncratic.

title: AIC: Batik Textiles of Java
description: This presentation explores the richly patterned wax-resist textiles known as batiks, their flourishing in the Indonesian island of Java, and their many inspirations and functions.

title: AIC: The Photographer's Curator: Hugh Edwards at the Art Institute of Chicago, 1959-1970
theme: The Photographer's Curator: Hugh Edwards at the Art Institute of Chicago, 1959-1970
description: As one of only a handful of American curators specializing in photography at that time, Hugh Edwards helped shape the field in Chicago and across the country.

title: AIC: Abstract Experiments: Latin American Art on Paper after 1950
theme: Abstract Experiments: Latin American Art on Paper after 1950
description: This exhibition explores a pivotal time in the development of abstraction in South America, as artists reimagined the international discourse on modernity in response to local concerns.

title: AIC: Provoke: Photography in Japan between Protest and Performance, 1960-1975
theme: Provoke: Photography in Japan between Protest and Performance, 1960-1975
description: This exhibition is the first to provide a thorough history of the Provoke movement and to draw out the many connections between photography, political protest, and performance in postwar Japan.

title: AIC: My Building, Your Design: Seven Portraits by David Hartt
theme: My Building, Your Design: Seven Portraits by David Hartt
description: Canadian David Hartt’s photographic series of iconic contemporary buildings explores the dichotomy between the daily experience of a building and the architect’s original design concept.

title: AIC: Volta Photo: Starring Sanlé Sory and the People of Bobo-Dioulasso in the Small but Musically Mighty Country of Burkina Faso
theme: Volta Photo: Starring Sanlé Sory and the People of Bobo-Dioulasso in the Small but Musically Mighty Country of Burkina Faso
description: This exhibition brings together photography and popular music of the West African country to present an immersive experience of a young nation negotiating its various identities.

title: AIC: Manet and the Sea
description: This landmark exhibition is devoted to the marine paintings of Edouard Manet (1832–1883), a little-studied but highly significant aspect of the career of the artist who is sometimes referred to as the father of Impressionism.

title: AIC: Toulouse-Lautrec and Montmartre
description: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec (1864–1901), one of the most popular and important painters of late-19th-century Paris, has not been the subject of a major exhibition since the large retrospective presented in London and Paris in 1991 and 1992. The National Gallery of Art and the Art Institute of Chicago have collaborated to organize Toulouse-Lautrec and Montmartre, an exhibition that places the artist's work at the peak of his career between 1888 and 1896 in conjunction with the work of other artists of the period.

title: AIC: Utamaro: Aspects of Beauty
description: This display includes some of the artist's most celebrated prints—portraits of pensive beauties, scenes of women engaged in everyday activities, and images of women of every age.

title:
AIC: Connoisseurship of Japanese Prints
 Part II: Contemporary Artists
theme:
Connoisseurship of Japanese Prints
 Part II: Contemporary Artists
description: Continuing with the theme of the previous exhibition which explored issues of connoisseurship in Edo period (1615-1868) prints, the current display tackles these questions for from the mid- to late 20th century.

title: AIC: Foreign Faces in Japanese Prints
description: Like people around the world, the Japanese of the Edo period (1615–1868) found foreigners fascinating, and woodblock print (ukiyo-e) artists and publishers were only too happy to accommodate the public’s appetite. Foreign Faces in Japanese Prints presents a range of works by some of the most prominent ukiyo-e artists of the 17th through 19th century, including Hishikawa Moronobu, Okumura Masanobu, Suzuki Harunobu, Kitagawa Utamaro, and Katsushika Hokusai. Printed books and lacquerware with foreign imagery are also on display.

title: AIC: The City as Image: The 1909 Plan of Chicago
theme: The City as Image: The 1909 Plan of Chicago
description: An integral part of the historic plan’s enduring influence, Jules Guérin’s monumental watercolors constitute a powerful pictorial narrative about the nature and goals of urban change.

title: AIC: Gates of the Lord: The Tradition of Krishna Paintings
theme: Gates of the Lord: The Tradition of Krishna Paintings
description: The first U.S. presentation of the art and aesthetics of the Pushtimarg sect of Hinduism, this exhibition features over 100 paintings and pichvais celebrating Shrinathji, a form of Krishna.

title: AIC: Undressed: The Fashion of Privacy
description: More than 120 drawings and prints, as well as works in other media, offer a behind-the-scenes perspective on dress and undress, the fascinating flip side of the very public face of high fashion.

title: AIC: Modern and Contemporary Works on Paper
theme: Modern and Contemporary Works on Paper
description: To herald the opening of the Modern Wing, the Department of Prints and Drawings will celebrate its extensive holdings of works on paper with an exhibition highlighting its modern and contemporary collection of drawings. Presenting approximately 80 works that, due to their inherent sensitivity to light, are rarely exhibited in public galleries, the exhibition shows artists’ evolving use of drawing, from highly finished works of art to notational and diagrammatic sheets.

title: AIC: The Floating World Emerges: Selections from the Clarence Buckingham Collection, Part I
theme: The Floating World Emerges: Selections from the Clarence Buckingham Collection, Part I
description: Featuring the museum’s earliest and most famous ukiyo-e prints, or “pictures of the floating world,” this exhibition includes approximately 35 works dating from the late 17th to the first half of the 18th century.

title: AIC: The Divine Art: Four Centuries of European Tapestries
theme: The Divine Art: Four Centuries of European Tapestries
description: For the first time in the history of the Art Institute, nearly all of its unparalleled tapestry collection is featured in a spectacular presentation. After decades in storage, these monumental artworks were subject to one of the largest tapestry conservation projects ever undertaken by a private workshop. Freshly conserved to their full splendor, The Divine Art's 70 masterpieces will only be on view for two months and then will return to storage, so be sure to catch these majestic works at their best—dazzling the eye beyond expectation.

title: AIC: Photography + Folk Art: Looking for America in the 1930s
theme: Photography + Folk Art: Looking for America in the 1930s
description: Over 100 works of photography, decorative arts, painting, sculpture, and textiles evidence the country’s search for, and eventual discovery of, a distinctly American character and vitality during the Great Depression.

title: AIC: Ink on Paper: Japanese Monochromatic Prints (2016)
theme: Ink on Paper: Japanese Monochromatic Prints
description: Spanning nearly 250 years, this selection of prints showcases the simple and striking use of dark ink on paper from the years before color printing.

title: AIC: A Field Guide to Photography and Media
theme: A Field Guide to Photography and Media
description: Celebrating the history and impact of photography through the Art Institute’s collection, this exhibition features more than 150 works that cut across time, space, and genre.

title: AIC: Picasso: Drawing from Life
description: Tracing over 70 years in the artist's prolific and varied practice, this selection of prints and drawings highlights the relationships that were integral to Picasso's career—from friends and lovers to dealers and printers—revealing not a solitary genius but an artist intimately connected to and buoyed by others.

title: AIC: Christina Ramberg: A Retrospective
description: This comprehensive exhibition includes Ramberg's well-known figural works as well as her lesser-known quilts, mid-career paintings, late abstractions, and ephemera from her informal archive.

title: AIC: Four Chicago Artists: Theodore Halkin, Evelyn Statsinger, Barbara Rossi, and Christina Ramberg
theme: Four Chicago Artists: Theodore Halkin, Evelyn Statsinger, Barbara Rossi, and Christina Ramberg
description: The exhibition brings together 95 works by four Chicago artists to showcase how their lives intersected across generations to shape the visual culture of our inimitable city.
